title: Spinach and Ricotta Cannelloni in Tomato Sauce
summary: Dried cannelloni tubes filled with a spinach and ricotta mixture, baked under tomato sauce, mozzarella and Parmesan until bubbling and golden.
equipment: piping bag or strong food bag with the corner snipped (or a teaspoon)

ingredients.item: Parmesan-style hard cheese (microbial rennet), finely grated
fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt
Parmesan-style hard cheese (microbial rennet), finely grated

steps.title: Wilt the spinach
steps.text: Wilt the spinach in a covered saucepan over medium heat for 3-4 minutes, using just the water clinging to the leaves and tossing once or twice. Once cool enough to handle, wring it out firmly in a tea towel until no more liquid runs out, since any leftover water would turn the filling runny. Chop the wrung spinach finely.

steps.title: Mix the filling
steps.text: While the spinach cools, drain the ricotta between two tea towels for 10 minutes to pull out excess whey. Combine the ricotta, chopped spinach, Parmesan, egg yolk, nutmeg, salt and pepper in a bowl until evenly mixed - the egg yolk helps bind everything so the filling holds its shape once baked.

steps.title: Make the tomato sauce
steps.text: Warm the olive oil with the garlic in a saucepan over medium-low heat for 2 minutes, just until the garlic turns pale gold without browning. Add the chopped tomatoes, passata, water and salt, and simmer for 10 minutes, then tear in the basil. The sauce should still look quite loose at this stage, since the dry cannelloni tubes will soak up liquid as they bake.

steps.title: Preheat the oven
steps.text: Preheat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan) at least 20 minutes ahead, so it reaches full temperature before the dish goes in.

steps.title: Fill the tubes
steps.text: Spread half the tomato sauce over the base of the baking dish. Pipe the ricotta and spinach filling into the dry cannelloni tubes using a piping bag or a food bag with the corner snipped off, then lay them in a single, snug layer over the sauce.

steps.title: Cover and top
steps.text: Pour the remaining sauce over the tubes so they're completely covered, as any exposed pasta will stay hard and chalky in the oven. Scatter the torn mozzarella and remaining Parmesan over the top.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Cover the dish with foil and bake for 30 minutes, then uncover and bake for a further 15-20 minutes, until bubbling and golden in patches. The pasta is done when a knife slides easily through a tube and an instant-read thermometer in the centre reads 74°C.

steps.title: Rest before serving
steps.text: Let the cannelloni rest for 10 minutes out of the oven before serving. This short rest allows the sauce to settle so it holds together on the plate rather than running everywhere.

tips: Wring the spinach out thoroughly - skipping this step is the most common cause of a watery filling that leaks out as the cannelloni bakes.
Keep the sauce on the loose side when assembling, since the uncooked tubes need that extra liquid to soften properly in the oven.
Make sure every tube is fully covered in sauce before baking; any exposed pasta tips will stay hard and pale.
Check the centre reaches 74°C with a thermometer before serving, especially if your dish is deeper or more tightly packed than usual.
storage: Leftovers keep covered in the fridge for up to 3 days, or can be frozen (baked or unbaked) for up to 2 months. Reheat in a 180°C oven until piping hot and the centre reaches 74°C, covering with foil if it's browning too quickly. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
